requirements.evidence: Covers nearly every requirement: migration matches the spec (unique entity_id+email, cascade, nullable invited_by); the model normalizes e-mail in both setEmailAttribute and creating; sendInvite validates, checks for existing members and pending invites, replaces expired/accepted invites in a transaction, turns QueryException into an inviteEmail error, and calls RateLimiter::hit only after success (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:55-125); PendingInvites accept is idempotent, rejects expired invites with an error on 'invite', uses firstOrCreate, sets the session and redirects; the route adds ->middleware('can:update,entity'); modals use ui.members_details and ui.members_remove_title with no wire:confirm; pending-invites.blade.php only renders <hr> when invites exist. Small gaps: the invite form relies on <x-input> to show the inviteEmail error (no explicit @error), which a test asserts renders exactly once; UserRole::manageable() is used in members.blade.php but is not in the diff, so I can't confirm it exists.

conventions.evidence: Positives: #[Validate] on the new properties, $this->authorize('update', ...) on actions, #[Fillable] on EntityInvite, a reversible migration with a generator-style timestamp, CHANGELOG/business-rules/database-schema/architecture docs updated, Bulma modals. Deviations: the domain writes (creating an invite, accepting an invite into a membership, changing roles) sit inline in the Livewire components rather than in app/Actions/* classes; the invitee check is a hand-rolled abort_if in PendingInvites::authorizeInvitee rather than a policy/gate; the CHANGELOG adds a stray blank line under ### Changed.

security.evidence: Every manager action calls authorize('update', $this->entity) and resolves IDs through entity-scoped relations (invites()->findOrFail, memberships()->findOrFail); the route and mount() both require update; accept/decline check the invitee e-mail before the idempotent return; output is escaped with {{ }}; rate limiting works. Minor gaps: selectedMembershipId is not #[Locked] (render/saveRole lookups are scoped, so impact is low); catching every QueryException can hide unrelated DB errors behind a 'duplicate invite' message.

tests.evidence: New tests in MembersTest, PendingInvitesTest, EntityInviteTest and EntityInviteMailTest cover: the invite happy path, validation including the owner role, duplicates and expired-invite replacement, the rate limit and that invalid input doesn't use quota, cancelling a foreign invite, employee 403 on both route and component, the error rendered exactly once, a foreign openMember throwing ModelNotFoundException, draft-only role changes, the owner/last-manager rules, the removal modal, accept/decline including non-invitee 403, idempotency, expiry, onboarding <hr> present/absent, the switcher, and the mail in en/pt_BR. Missing: a test for the unique-constraint race (QueryException path) and a tamper test on selectedMembershipId.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct and reuses existing relations and policies. Some extra or speculative code: e-mail normalization is done twice (setEmailAttribute plus the creating hook in EntityInvite.php), sendInvite lowercases the e-mail by hand as well, and scopeAccepted(), invitedBy(), the factory accepted() state and the empty attachments() boilerplate are not required.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, comments are short and helpful ("A concurrent request won the unique (entity_id, email) index."), and the style matches sibling files. sendInvite runs about 70 lines and would read better if it were extracted into an Action.

scope.evidence: Adds .github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml and .github/workflows/tests.yml (a deploy pipeline with HOSTINGER_API secrets), which have nothing to do with invites. Dropping the employee 'Members' link from dashboard.blade.php and moving the navbar link under @can('update') are justified by the manager-only requirement.

issues.explanation: Adds CI/deploy workflows, including a VPS deploy job using secrets, that are unrelated to the invite feature and should not be in this PR.
Domain writes (create invite, accept invite into membership, save role) live in Livewire components rather than app/Actions/* use-case classes as the conventions require.
The invitee check is a hand-rolled abort_if instead of a policy/gate, which conflicts with 'authorization always goes through policies/gates'.
Catching every QueryException reports any DB failure as 'already invited' instead of only unique-constraint violations.
The unique-constraint race path (QueryException turned into an inviteEmail error) is not tested, and there is no tamper test setting selectedMembershipId to a foreign membership before saveRole.
UserRole::manageable() is used but not defined in the diff, so whether it exists can't be verified from the change.
selectedMembershipId is server-selected context but is not #[Locked]; lookups are entity-scoped, so the impact is low.
E-mail normalization is duplicated in the creating hook and the mutator, and scopeAccepted/invitedBy/accepted() are unused extras.
A stray blank line separates the new ### Changed entry from the existing entries.

review.summary: The change replaces instant member-adding with an invite flow: a new entity_invites table and model, a queued markdown invite mail, a PendingInvites component on the switcher and onboarding pages, and a manager-only members page with a role-detail modal and a removal-confirmation modal, backed by broad tests and doc updates. The functionality and security are solid, but the PR adds unrelated CI/deploy workflow files and keeps domain writes in components instead of app/Actions, so it needs changes before merging.
